properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 2:48AM MDT until October 27 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

For the Upper Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 AM MDT Monday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 AM MDT Monday was 9.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.0 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.0
feet on 05/23/1948.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 300 PM MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 7:44PM MDT until October 29 at 8:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are
being flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been
this high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also
be flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:00 PM MDT Sunday the stage was 20.0 feet. No reliable
observations available thereafter.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum known river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 3:00 PM MDT Sunday was 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 24.2 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Jemez River Above Jemez Pueblo affecting Sandoval County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Jemez River above Jemez Pueblo.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, multiple locations along Highway 4 between
San Ysidro and Jemez Springs will see water crossing the road from
tributaries and low water crossing points. The Wastewater Treatment
plant 1 mile downstream of Jemez Springs can be impacted between 7
and 7.7 feet. Water will be on Highway 4 at mile marker 1, 2 and
13.  Homes near the river in San Ysidro could be impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:45 PM MDT Sunday the stage was 5.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.2 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 9:25PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to continue to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage
early this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Sunday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 1:27PM MST until October 26 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Birdsprings to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MST /1000 AM MDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 111 PM MST /211 PM MDT/, water levels have fallen below action
stage at Winslow and will continue to fall this afternoon.
However, downstream impacts will continue near Birdsprings
through Monday morning.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 1:00pm MST /2:00pm MDT/ the stage was 16.94 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels have fallen below action stage and will
continue to fall through this afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Birdsprings will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow.

- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
